claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's lovely to meet you, and I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask a few more questions:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Now, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I understand Alex doesn't currently live with you.

Could you tell me a bit more about Alex's living situation? For example:

- Is he living with another family member or friend?
- Is he in local authority care?
- Is he in hospital or residential accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in local authority care for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I appreciate this may be a difficult situation.

Since Alex has been in local authority care for a few months, I have a couple of follow-up questions:

1. Has Alex been in care for more than 8 weeks?

2. Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's been in care for more than 8 weeks. And no, he doesn't come home to stay with me - he's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. I have one more question that may be relevant:

Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he is in care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what you mean - could you clarify? Alex is in local authority care, so the council is looking after him there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course, I apologise for any confusion.

What I mean is: since Alex is in local authority care, the local council is typically responsible for paying for his accommodation and day-to-day needs (like food, clothing, etc.) while he's there. Is that the case for Alex - is the council covering those costs for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - the council covers all of that while he's in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks
- Alex does not spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you
- The local council is paying for his accommodation and maintenance

Unfortunately, based on these circumstances, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. Let me explain why and provide you with the official outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to let you know that based on the information you've provided, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 8):**
- Under Child Benefit rules, when a child has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, eligibility for Child Benefit usually ends.
- There is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, but since Alex is in the care home full-time, this exception does not apply.
- Additionally, because the local council is paying for Alex's accommodation and maintenance, you would not normally qualify.

**If your circumstances change:**
If Alex's situation changes in the future - for example, if he starts spending at least 2 nights in a row each week at home, or 7 or more consecutive days at home - you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. In that case, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to discuss your options.

I understand this may not be the news you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help you with?
